title: US sets out five-point European security plan before Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi
dek: Jared Kushner said no country would have a veto over another's alliances. Russia fired ballistic missiles at Kyiv on Saturday, three days before the talks open.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
The United States has put forward a five-point framework for European security as part of its push to end the war in Ukraine, its envoy Jared Kushner said after talks in Brussels with Ukrainian, NATO and European officials, days before the first three-way US-Russia-Ukraine talks since February.

The Kremlin said on Friday that no European proposals on security guarantees had reached Moscow. "As for any proposals from the Europeans, none have reached us, and we are not aware of any," spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters, according to Russian state media.

## What Kushner proposed

In a statement posted on X on Thursday, Kushner said the US had held "productive and substantive discussions" in Brussels with Ukraine, NATO and European partners on "two essential and interlinked elements of a lasting peace: security guarantees for Ukraine and a broader European security architecture". The meeting brought together a Ukrainian delegation and representatives of France, Britain, Germany, the US and NATO, reports said.

The framework, as described in his statement and in reports, has five elements:

- permanent security consultations
- reliable channels of crisis communication
- greater military transparency
- reciprocal measures to reduce the risk of escalation
- a lasting framework for European security and stability

Kushner said each country would keep authority over its own security and alliances and "no country would have a veto over another's sovereign choices", and that NATO "will remain central to European collective defense". He said the US would "also engage Russia as part of the peace negotiations" and that the aim was "to address the security concerns of all sides through practical, mutually agreed arrangements that reduce the risk of future conflict". No agreement on the proposals has been announced.

## Abu Dhabi next week

Kushner confirmed that the United States will convene talks with Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi next week. US envoy Steve Witkoff said on 3 November that the US would mediate working-group-level negotiations on 10 and 11 November, focused on "post-war security arrangements, de-escalation, humanitarian efforts, and the next steps toward achieving peace".

Peskov said on Tuesday that Europe could not join the Abu Dhabi round because "a trilateral format was coordinated" between Russia and Ukraine with US mediation, and that the Russian delegation would be led by presidential aide Vladimir Medinsky. On Saturday Peskov said Igor Kostyukov, head of Russia's military intelligence agency, would also travel to Abu Dhabi, according to Russian news agencies. Reports said the Russian team would include Deputy Foreign Ministers Sergei Ryabkov and Mikhail Galuzin and Yuri Zhigarlovsky, a senior officer of the General Staff, alongside other military and diplomatic officials. Kyiv had not named its delegation by Saturday afternoon. Security guarantees would be discussed, he said, but "these can only be mutual". Moscow has long said that the expansion of NATO is a root cause of the war, a position Kyiv and its Western backers reject.

Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky held a 90-minute call with Kushner and Witkoff on Wednesday, reports said. He has said that any post-war security guarantees for Ukraine must be "binding and enforceable", and has pressed Washington for more Patriot air-defence interceptors. The two sides remain far apart on terms, including what protection Ukraine would have and how the West would respond if Russia attacked again, reports said.

Fighting continues. Russian forces launched a missile attack on Kyiv early on Saturday, three days before the Abu Dhabi talks are due to open. Mayor Vitali Klitschko said on Telegram that the enemy was "hitting infrastructure with ballistic missiles", and that debris damaged a five-storey apartment building in a western district of the city and the facade of another residential building. The city's military administration said two people were injured and a building housing a kindergarten was damaged. Russia's defence ministry had not commented by Saturday morning. In his nightly address on Friday, President Zelensky had warned that Russia was preparing new attacks on energy targets, bridges and other infrastructure, according to reports.

More broadly, Russia keeps striking Ukrainian cities and energy infrastructure, Ukrainian officials say; Russia says it targets military and energy facilities. Neither side's figures can be independently verified.

## Why it matters for India

India has called for dialogue and diplomacy throughout the war and keeps close ties with both Moscow and Kyiv. It is one of the largest buyers of Russian crude oil, so any settlement that eases Western sanctions on Russia would affect what Indian refiners pay and how they pay for it. A deal would also matter to the Indian families whose relatives are still serving with the Russian armed forces; the Ministry of External Affairs says it keeps raising their release with Moscow. The UAE, host of next week's talks, is one of India's closest partners in the Gulf.

## What happens next

The Abu Dhabi talks are due on 10 and 11 November. Consultations on the European security framework are to continue with Ukraine, NATO, the European Union and other European partners, according to reports of the US proposal.
